beats.narration_text: Hello. I'm Arundhati Kandelkar, a master's student at Northeastern.
beats.motion_claim: My name and programme type in while I say them.

qc.sparse_reason: Name card: the name is the whole picture.

beats.narration_text: I'm building Co-op Sponsor Check: a tool that tells international students whether a company has ever sponsored someone for a software job.

show.event: types 'I'm building Co-op Sponsor Check' as it is spoken

beats.motion_claim: The one-sentence summary types in as it is spoken.

qc.sparse_reason: One-sentence summary card.

beats.narration_text: When international students like me pick an internship, we need to know one thing: has this company ever sponsored someone for a software job? Today we guess, and a missing record looks like a no. My tool says I don't know, instead of guessing no.

show.event: corrects 'sponsor visas' to the narrower question

props.replacementWords: have a record of sponsoring software jobs

beats.motion_claim: The naive question is corrected to the one a tool can answer.

qc.sparse_reason: Hesitant-writer bookend: the correction is the motion.

beats.narration_text: When it's done, it will be a public GitHub repository: the tool, a twenty-five company evaluation set, and a log of where it fails.

beats.narration_text: Part two. What already exists?
beats.motion_claim: Part title types in as it is spoken.

qc.sparse_reason: Part title card: the structure the assignment asks for.

beats.narration_text: The official source is the U S C I S, H-1B Employer Data Hub. When I searched it for Capital One, it listed two employers, Capital One National Association, and Capital One Services. My dataset has neither. But the hub is searched one employer at a time, and it has no job-title filter.

shot.visual_intent: A search window with the query 'Capital One' and the two employer names the hub listed; beside it a 'job title' filter pill gets crossed out; tag 'MY SEARCH · uscis.gov · 2026-10-25'.
shot.motion_claim: A search window with the query 'Capital One' and the two employer names the hub listed; beside it a 'job title' filter pill gets crossed out; tag 'MY SEARCH · uscis.gov · 2026-10-25'.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn object or scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, the voice carrying the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: I also searched Open Sanctions, a database for sanctions and risk screening, for Robinhood, Chime, and So Fi. Chime returned eleven results, mostly unrelated people, and Chime Financial was not among the ones I reviewed. It shows how a brand-name search returns related or irrelevant matches.

shot.visual_intent: A search window with the query 'Chime' and a column of eleven result rows, mostly greyed person rows; a crossed-out 'Chime Financial Inc' label beside it; tag 'MY SEARCH · opensanctions.org'.

show.event: 'Chime Financial Inc' crossed: not in the results

shot.motion_claim: A search window with the query 'Chime' and a column of eleven result rows, mostly greyed person rows; a crossed-out 'Chime Financial Inc' label beside it; tag 'MY SEARCH · opensanctions.org'.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn object or scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, the voice carrying the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: Then G L E I F, the global register of legal entity identifiers. It connected brand names to legal names: Robinhood to Robinhood Markets, and So Fi to Social Finance, L L C, which was once Social Finance, Inc.

shot.visual_intent: Two brand tags on the left, arrows to the legal names GLEIF listed on the right: ROBINHOOD MARKETS, INC. and SOCIAL FINANCE, LLC with 'previously SOCIAL FINANCE, INC.'; tag 'MY SEARCH · gleif.org'.
shot.motion_claim: Two brand tags on the left, arrows to the legal names GLEIF listed on the right: ROBINHOOD MARKETS, INC. and SOCIAL FINANCE, LLC with 'previously SOCIAL FINANCE, INC.'; tag 'MY SEARCH · gleif.org'.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn object or scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, the voice carrying the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: But neither tool is built to find employers that sponsor H-1B visas. Finding them takes time, especially when a company's brand name is different from its legal name in the data. My tool brings that information together, finds possible name variations, and lets you verify the result, instead of blindly trusting an automatic match.

shot.visual_intent: One brand tag 'Chime' with lines to two legal-name tags; a 'you verify' check box lands between them.

show.event: brand tag and two legal names

beats.narration_text: Here is what exists today. On October third I pushed a recipe to my fork of the Reallocation Engine. It takes a company and the job I want, software or full-stack development.

shot.visual_intent: A kraft company box drops onto the stage beside a flat data page; tag 'EXISTS · 03784b0'.
shot.motion_claim: A kraft company box drops onto the stage beside a flat data page; tag 'EXISTS · 03784b0'.

beats.narration_text: For each company it checks three things. Is there a record of sponsoring software titles? Does the co-op start before graduation? And is the job posting still live?

shot.visual_intent: The box opens; a record page, a calendar block and a check rise out of it, one per question.
shot.motion_claim: The box opens; a record page, a calendar block and a check rise out of it, one per question.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn object or scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, the voice carrying the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: When a company is missing from the data, it does not treat that as zero. It says unknown, and tells you to ask a person.

shot.visual_intent: A box rides up to a gate; the gate shows a question mark, never a zero.
shot.motion_claim: A box rides up to a gate; the gate shows a question mark, never a zero.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn object or scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, the voice carrying the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: The data comes from a public dataset built from a list of funded startups taken from S E C filings. That is its biggest limit: the big banks are not in it at all.

shot.visual_intent: A data page with a gap; three bank boxes drop toward it and pass through the gap.
shot.motion_claim: A data page with a gap; three bank boxes drop toward it and pass through the gap.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn object or scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, the voice carrying the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: Today I fixed brand names. If what you type is the first word of a company's name, like Chime, the tool now lists Chime Financial and Chime Inc. If the legal name shares no word, like So Fi, a short alias list I wrote points to Social Finance. Either way a person picks. Twenty-six tests pass.

shot.visual_intent: Typed 'Chime' fans out to two rows; typed 'SoFi' goes through an alias arrow to 'SOCIAL FINANCE INC'; a 'human check' box lands; tag 'BUILT · 2026-11-23 · 26 tests'.
shot.motion_claim: Typed 'Chime' fans out to two rows; typed 'SoFi' goes through an alias arrow to 'SOCIAL FINANCE INC'; a 'human check' box lands; tag 'BUILT · 2026-11-23 · 26 tests'.

beats.narration_text: Next, the official hub becomes a second data source, so a missing bank becomes a real answer or an honest unknown. Then a written failure analysis, and a README with a one-command demo.

beats.narration_text: What do I need? I have what I need to build and test this: my laptop, Python, GitHub, the public U S C I S data, and Claude Code access through Northeastern. I don't need paid AI credits, because the tool doesn't use an AI model at run time.

beats.narration_text: Part four. How will I know it worked?
beats.motion_claim: Part title types in as it is spoken.

qc.sparse_reason: Part title card: the structure the assignment asks for.

beats.narration_text: I test it on twenty-five companies. Every company I looked up in the official hub was there. In October my tool found a record for only two. It never guessed no. But that number told me something was wrong.

shot.visual_intent: A grid of twenty-five company squares; all fill grey and rows land in the results table; two get terracotta dots; tag '25 RAN · 2026-10-12 / 10-25'.
shot.motion_claim: A grid of twenty-five company squares; all fill grey and rows land in the results table; two get terracotta dots; tag '25 RAN · 2026-10-12 / 10-25'.

beats.narration_text: Two real problems. First, my matcher turned Goldman Sachs and Co, L L C, into Goldman Sachs and. It is fixed now, with a test that failed before the fix and passes after.

shot.visual_intent: The hub's name 'GOLDMAN SACHS AND CO LLC', an arrow, and the matcher's output 'GOLDMAN SACHS' with a tick; tag 'FIXED · 2026-10-24'.
shot.motion_claim: The hub's name 'GOLDMAN SACHS AND CO LLC', an arrow, and the matcher's output 'GOLDMAN SACHS' with a tick; tag 'FIXED · 2026-10-24'.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn object or scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, the voice carrying the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: Second, brand names: Robinhood, Chime and So Fi were missed. Before fixing it, I predicted the first-word rule would catch two, and So Fi would need the alias. That is what happened. Now none of the three is missed, six of the twenty-five go to a person, and there are no wrong automatic answers.

shot.visual_intent: A before/after table with three rows: missed strong sponsors 3 → 0, wrong automatic answers 1 → 0, sent to a person 0 → 6; tag 'MEASURED · 2026-11-23 · predictions first'.
shot.motion_claim: A before/after table with three rows: missed strong sponsors 3 → 0, wrong automatic answers 1 → 0, sent to a person 0 → 6; tag 'MEASURED · 2026-11-23 · predictions first'.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn object or scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, the voice carrying the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: After I add the hub, I'll consider it successful if at least twenty of the twenty-five companies get a verified match, with zero incorrect automatic sponsor answers. Anything uncertain must stay unknown, or go to a person. It fails if it confirms a wrong company, or if the second source does not improve coverage.

shot.visual_intent: Two columns, PASS and FAIL: PASS = at least 20 of 25 verified, 0 wrong automatic answers, uncertain stays unknown or goes to a person; FAIL = a wrong company confirmed, no better coverage; tag 'MY TARGET · after the hub is added'.
